Consider the basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ (shown above) and a basis $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3.$
The matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the linear map $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ relative to these bases, and the vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^2,$ are also given. Find $[\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})]_{\mathcal{C}}.$
question.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $\mathbf{x}$ under $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}},$ the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{B}.$ So, let

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14157119/assets/a244da85e128687b438d43ee49c8ee5b0bf864c0b36add61c382a7dff70dad66.svg)

This gives us the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=5 \\ 4{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 4 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14157119/assets/ef57f78641f939448e504b4ada6d538fef7a2800f130badb5c4970e3d2b1d4d1.svg)

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 \\ -9 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
